data.narrative:
HawkEye 360 is a Series D+ space and aerospace company that has raised $300M+ to date. The valuation exercise draws on a broader comp universe of 13 peers—5 public-market comparables (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private-stage competitors including SpaceX, Rocket Lab, ICEYE, Sierra Space, and Planet Labs—though no narrow peer set at identical stage and valuation tier exists.

Standard triangulation methods encounter material constraints. Peer-median analysis is inapplicable: while 14 same-sector peers exist in Space & Aerospace, zero narrow-filter datapoints (same-stage, adjacent-stage, similar-valuation-tier combinations) meet the minimum threshold of three comparables. Public-comp anchoring via price-to-sales multiples is likewise unavailable; the public Space & Aerospace median trades at 27.4x revenue across the five tickers noted, but HawkEye 360's revenue is not disclosed—a structural limitation for private companies.

Without disclosed revenue or a sufficiently granular peer cohort, quantitative triangulation cannot be responsibly completed. Any valuation estimate would require either: (1) non-public revenue data, (2) acceptance of wide-band multiples applied to estimated revenue, or (3) reliance on precedent transaction or investor signaling outside the scope of this analysis. The $300M+ capital raised to date provides a floor, but does not itself establish current post-money valuation. Further diligence on comparable transaction multiples or explicit revenue traction is required to narrow the range.
